subject: Cognitive Science
title: Operant Conditioning
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Operant Conditioning.

hook.text: A rat presses a lever and gets food. It presses again. And again. Consequences shape behavior.

buildup.text: B.F. Skinner showed that rewards increase behavior and punishments decrease it. Simple but powerful.

discovery.text: There are four types: positive reinforcement, negative reinforcement, positive punishment, negative punishment.

twist.text: Intermittent rewards are more addictive than constant ones. Slot machines exploit this perfectly.

climax.text: Every app notification, every gamified badge, every sales bonus uses Skinner's principles.

quiz.question: Why are intermittent rewards more powerful than constant ones?

details.summary: Skinner showed that behavior is shaped by its consequences. Reinforcement increases behavior; punishment decreases it. Positive reinforcement adds something rewarding; negative reinforcement removes something aversive. Schedules of reinforcement determine how persistent the learned behavior becomes.
details.whyItMatters: Operant conditioning governs much of voluntary behavior. Understanding reinforcement schedules explains habit formation, addiction, and effective behavior management.
takeaways: Consequences shape the probability of future behavior
Reinforcement increases behavior; punishment decreases it
Variable schedules produce the most persistent behavior

faq.question: What is the difference between positive and negative reinforcement?
faq.answer: Positive reinforcement adds a reward after behavior, like praise for good work. Negative reinforcement removes an unpleasant condition, like taking aspirin to relieve a headache. Both increase the target behavior. Negative reinforcement is not punishment; it still makes behavior more likely.

faq.question: Why are variable reinforcement schedules so powerful?
faq.answer: Variable schedules deliver rewards unpredictably, creating high, steady response rates and strong resistance to extinction. Slot machines, social media notifications, and fishing all use variable reinforcement. The unpredictability keeps the organism engaged because the next response might pay off.
